understanding the neural mechanisms underlying the development and maintenance of drug dependence.
the neural substrates underlying abstinence-induced cravings for cigarettes in chronic smokers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
abstinence from nicotine results in increased activation in the OFC/ACC and that this increased activation is associated with craving.
the neural substrates underlying abstinence-induced cigarette cravings in chronic smokers include regions of the brain's reward circuitry and the visuospatial system.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
abstinence-induced cravings for cigarettes are associated with increased activity in brain regions involved in reward and visuospatial processing.
abstinence from smoking, and associated craving, is associated with increased activity in a network that includes the ventral striatum, insula, thalamus and hippocampus.

The main takeaway from our work is that
abstinence from smoking is associated with increased activity in the anterior cingulate and orbitofrontal cortices, which are important for decision-making and impulse control.
abstinence from nicotine (and presumably other drugs of abuse) is associated with increased brain activity in the brain's reward and visuospatial processing circuitry.
